title: group_oscore: epoch semantics not wrap/grace coherent (validate_epoch, key_valid_at, id_context collision)
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/group_oscore.py. Three coherent problems: (1) validate_epoch (:137-148) rejects every epoch < current immediately, but spec 18.8.2 (spec/12-apps.md:1218) says old key_epoch is rejected only AFTER a 1-hour grace period — grace lives only in key_valid_at; two exported predicates encode contradictory acceptance policy. (2) Wrap unsafety: at current=0xFFFFFFFF the true successor (epoch 1, what rekey emits) is numerically < current -> rejected as rollback; key_valid_at tests material.epoch == self._current.epoch and key_for_epoch searches by number (:160,166), so after wrap the original epoch-1 material becomes unresolvable and the original epoch-max material reads future_epoch_unknown; test_wrap_boundary_validation (test_group_oscore.py:101-105) blesses the inconsistency instead of pinning the laggard side. (3) id_context = group_id||epoch collides across wrap (epoch 2 recurs): if key material were ever reused across the wrap boundary, nonce reuse gives full plaintext recovery. Fix: wrap-aware comparison via wrap-generation counting or distance metric; identity compare (material is self._current) in key_valid_at; drop/replace _previous entries whose epoch would collide on wrap; mix wrap generation into id_context or document never-reuse as an invariant; add the laggard-side test; reconcile validate_epoch with the grace window or explicitly document the split.
